description: Critical tasks for the first 48-72 hours after a death

tasks.title: Obtain death certificates
tasks.description: Order 10-15 certified copies of the death certificate from the funeral home or vital records office. These are required for nearly every official notification and claim.
tasks.why_it_matters: Banks, insurance companies, government agencies, and financial institutions all require certified copies. Getting enough upfront saves time and additional trips to vital records.
tips: Order more copies than you think you need—10-15 is typical
Certified copies cost $10-25 each depending on the state
The funeral home can usually order these for you
Some institutions accept photocopies, but most require certified originals
Keep track of which institutions keep the certificate vs. return it
tasks.estimated_time: 30 minutes to order, 1-2 weeks to receive

tasks.title: Notify immediate family and close friends
tasks.description: Contact close family members and friends who need to know. Consider delegating some calls to a trusted family member to share the load.
tasks.why_it_matters: Close family and friends deserve to hear the news directly, not through social media or other channels. They may also want to help with arrangements.
tips: It's okay to ask someone else to make some of these calls for you
Have a brief script ready if that helps
It's okay to send texts if phone calls feel too overwhelming
Consider creating a phone tree where each person calls 2-3 others
You don't need to have all the details—it's okay to say 'I don't know yet'

tasks.title: Contact funeral home and make arrangements
tasks.description: Choose a funeral home and begin making arrangements for burial or cremation. If your loved one had pre-planned arrangements, locate those documents.
tasks.why_it_matters: Funeral arrangements need to happen quickly, especially if there will be a viewing. Pre-planned arrangements may already be paid for.
tips: Ask if your loved one left any written wishes about their service
You can negotiate funeral costs—get itemized pricing
The FTC Funeral Rule requires funeral homes to provide price lists
Consider having a trusted friend or family member accompany you
It's okay to take a day before making decisions if you need time

tasks.title: Secure the deceased's home
tasks.description: If your loved one lived alone, secure their home immediately. Change locks if keys are unaccounted for, check that all doors and windows are locked, and ensure valuables are safe.
tasks.why_it_matters: Unfortunately, home break-ins after a death (especially after obituaries are published) do happen. Securing the property protects belongings and the estate.
tips: Collect mail regularly to prevent it from piling up
Set lights on timers to make the home look occupied
Ask a neighbor to keep an eye on the property
Don't announce funeral times in obituaries—this tells burglars when the home will be empty
Consider removing obvious valuables temporarily

tasks.title: Locate will and important documents
tasks.description: Find the original will, trust documents, life insurance policies, and other critical paperwork. Check home safes, safe deposit boxes, filing cabinets, and with their attorney.
tasks.why_it_matters: The will names the executor and contains burial wishes. Life insurance policies may have time limits for filing. These documents guide all future decisions.
tips: Check with their attorney, accountant, or financial advisor
Look for a safe deposit box key—check their bank
Search email for insurance companies, attorneys, or financial advisors
Check for a fireproof safe at their home
Some people store important documents with a trusted family member

tasks.title: Notify the deceased's employer
tasks.description: If your loved one was employed, contact their HR department to notify them of the death. Ask about final paychecks, benefits, life insurance through work, and any personal belongings.
tasks.why_it_matters: The employer may owe final wages, vacation pay, or death benefits. Many employers offer life insurance as a benefit that families don't know about.
tips: Ask about any life insurance through the employer
Inquire about 401(k) or pension benefits
Ask about COBRA health insurance continuation if applicable
Request any personal items from their workspace
Ask about any unpaid wages, bonuses, or commissions owed

tasks.title: Arrange care for pets
tasks.description: If your loved one had pets, ensure they are being cared for. This may be temporary until permanent arrangements can be made.
tasks.why_it_matters: Pets need immediate care and can be a source of comfort during grief. Making permanent arrangements can wait, but immediate needs cannot.
tips: Check if the will mentions arrangements for pets
Ask family members if anyone can take them temporarily or permanently
Locate veterinary records for any ongoing medications
Gather pet supplies from the deceased's home
Consider if keeping the pet might be comforting for a surviving spouse

tasks.title: Notify doctors and cancel medical appointments
tasks.description: Contact the deceased's primary care physician and any specialists to inform them of the death and cancel upcoming appointments.
tasks.why_it_matters: This prevents appointment reminders and ensures medical records are updated. If hospice was involved, they can help with this process.
tips: Ask for copies of medical records if needed for insurance claims
Cancel any prescription auto-refills
Return any rented medical equipment (hospital beds, oxygen, etc.)
Ask about any outstanding medical bills
